title: DP-1 Extension Registry
description: Official registry of DP-1 protocol extensions

extensions.name: Channel Extension
extensions.description: Collaborative, persistent feeds of playlists with enhanced metadata and curation capabilities. Adds multi-curator support, publisher attribution, verifiable identities, and multi-signature roles including publisher. Conforming players verify feed and publisher signatures per the extension spec (rules are documented in prose, not enforced by the JSON Schema). Curators and publisher use the one DP-1 Entity model, defined in the core Ref Manifest schema and shared with the Playlist Extension and metadata.artists[].
features: Multi-curator exhibitions with verifiable identities
Publisher attribution for institutions and collectives
DID-based entity format (curators and publisher); key is optional and informational, so a partner organization without a DID is named by name and links

One Entity model: curators[] and publisher $ref the core Ref Manifest $defs/Entity, so they carry role, location, addresses, avatar, biographies and links exactly as an artist does (url deprecated in favour of a links entry of type profile or website). schema.json is therefore no longer self-contained: compiling it requires resolving the core ref-manifest schema
Multi-signature support (aligned with DP-1 v1.1.0), including `publisher` as a signature role alongside curator, feed, agent, institution, and licensor

Player verification: conforming implementations MUST verify at least one `feed` and one `publisher` signature before accepting a channel (specified in channel.md; JSON Schema validates structure and role enum only)
Enhanced metadata (summary, coverImage)

extensions.name: Playlist Extension
extensions.description: Extensions to DP-1 playlists for dynamic item fetching, enhanced metadata, optional experimental Note (intermission) fields, displayAt scheduling (item-level displayAt; activates automatically when any item has displayAt), inline carriage of the standardized Ref Manifest on items (inlineManifest), playlist-level visibility (unlisted playlists stay out of directory listings), and the editorial and identity fields a gallery needs (the shared Entity model for curators and note authors, playlist-level links[] and openAt, and a note title and author). Enables playlists to transition from static collections to live, personalized, and time-filtered feeds.
features: Dynamic query for real-time item fetching from indexers
Multiple resolution profiles (graphql-v1, https-json-v1)
Template variable hydration ({{viewer_address}}, {{chain}}, etc.)
Response mapping with schema validation
Curator metadata with DID-based verifiable identities (key optional and informational)

One Entity model: $defs/Entity $refs the core Ref Manifest $defs/Entity, so a curator, partner or note author carries role, location, addresses, avatar, biographies and links exactly as an artist does; the channels extension references the same definition, so the two cannot drift

Playlist-level links[]: editorial content about the playlist — articles, events, news — in display order, each a core $defs/Link carrying title, date, thumbnail and authors so a consumer draws a card from the entry alone; references only, the content stays at the URL

Playlist-level openAt: when the playlist's subject became public (an exhibition's opening), reusing DisplayAt's wire shape for one date format but outside §3.5 displayAt Scheduling — no eligibility, no timer, no activation — and distinct from created, which churns on re-export
Note title and author: an optional heading (1-200 characters) and an Entity who wrote the text; omitting author means the note is the curators' own
Enhanced metadata (summary, coverImage)
Fast start, rich upgrade rendering strategy
Experimental Note (intermission): optional short artist-authored text with optional display duration on the playlist and on each item; extension-only (allOf overlay), not canonical DP-1 core

displayAt scheduling: automatically active when any item has displayAt; playback includes only the current release (latest past displayAt instant) plus items without displayAt (ISO 8601; bare local = display locale, Z/offset absolute; date-only not accepted); transitions apply immediately

Inline Manifest: a full Ref Manifest document carried on a PlaylistItem as inlineManifest — same schema and validation as a ref-fetched manifest, ref overrides inline, integrity via the playlist signature (no refHash needed)

Visibility: optional signed playlist-level visibility (public, the default, or unlisted); directories list a playlist only when visibility is absent or public, container listings may include an unlisted playlist the container names; a listing request, not access control

extensions.name: Content Rating Extension
extensions.description: Signed, per-item audience labels for playlist items: an optional contentRating with defined values general and mature (absence, or a value a consumer does not recognize, is unrated; nothing is assumed from an unknown label) and optional open-vocabulary contentReasons in the curator's own words. Defines the label and its meaning only; viewer policy (what a device hides, and who may change that) is a consumer concern. Filtered playback is a projection, never a re-signed document; contentBlocked is reserved for valid documents a consumer's policy fully excludes.
features: Per-item contentRating: defined values general | mature; absence or an unrecognized value means unrated, so the vocabulary is open on the wire and only mature hides anything
Per-item contentReasons: open-vocabulary non-empty strings; explanatory, never a filtering taxonomy
Overlay on PlaylistItem via allOf; canonical core playlist.json unchanged; composes with the Playlist Extension v0.2.0 (four composed schemas, one shared $defs/PlaylistItemExtension)
Consumer rules: filtering is a consumer concern; a filtered projection is never presented as signed and signatures verify on the original bytes; non-aware consumers accept and ignore the fields
Reserved player error code contentBlocked for a valid document whose items are all excluded by consumer policy; malformed labels remain playlistInvalid
Scope boundary: audience suitability (for whom, age ranges) is reserved for a separate future audience field on playlists and channels, never as new contentRating values

changes: Channel and Playlist extensions: one Entity model. Both now $ref $defs/Entity in the core Ref Manifest schema (refVersion 1.2.0) instead of keeping their own copies, so curators, partners, publishers and note authors carry the same fields as metadata.artists[]: optional role (artist | curator | partner | sponsor | publisher | other), location, addresses, avatar, biographies and links, with url deprecated.

Channel and Playlist extensions: key is no longer required on an entity. It is informational only (channel.md §5.3, MUST relaxed to SHOULD), so a partner organization with no DID is named by name and links rather than a placeholder. Loosening: every document valid before this change stays valid, but a validator built on the previous shape rejects a keyless entity.

Channel and Playlist extensions: neither schema.json is self-contained any more. Compiling either one requires resolving https://dp1.feralfile.com/schemas/v1.1.0/ref-manifest.json, which the Playlist Extension already required for inlineManifest and the Channel Extension did not.

Playlist extension: optional playlist-level links[] (§3.3.1) for editorial content — articles, events, news — in display order, and optional playlist-level openAt (§3.4) for when the subject became public. openAt reuses DisplayAt's wire shape for one date format but takes no part in §3.5 displayAt Scheduling and sets no eligibility.
Playlist extension: note gains an optional title (1-200 characters) and author (an Entity).

Core: Link.type gains profile, publication, article, event and news, and Link gains optional title, date, thumbnail and authors, so a consumer renders a link as a card without fetching the page. controls gains permissions (camera, microphone), controls.display and DisplayPrefs gain imageRendering (auto | pixelated), metadata.medium carries a closed-enumeration type plus details[], and provenance.contract.seriesId accepts a decimal string as well as an integer.

Channel extension: version and schema $id move to v1.1.0 (.../extensions/channels/v1.1.0/schema.json). Adopting the live $ref means a released $id would no longer denote stable content — the core Ref Manifest is edited in place, so every later additive edit to its Entity, Link or Thumbnail definitions would change what validates under the published identifier. v1.0.0 stands as published; see channel.md §13 for the entry and §10.1 for the SemVer rule it follows (Minor: additive, backward-compatible).

Playlist extension: unchanged at draft v0.2.0 with its $id unchanged, per playlist.md §8.1 draft amendments, and recorded as a dated amendment in its own §11. Core stays 1.1.0 with a spec §16 Editorial entry.

Playlist extension: optional top-level visibility (public, the default when absent, or unlisted). Directories list a playlist only when visibility is absent or exactly public and treat any other value as unlisted; a channel or group naming an unlisted playlist may still list it among its members. Inside the signed bytes; a listing request, not access control.
Playlist extension: schema accepts any string for visibility (open vocabulary, as in content-rating); canonical core playlist.json unchanged; status remains draft extension v0.2.0.

Registered Content Rating Extension v0.1.0 (draft): per-item contentRating (defined values general | mature; absence or an unrecognized value is unrated) and open-vocabulary contentReasons on PlaylistItem, as an allOf overlay; canonical core playlist.json unchanged.

Content Rating extension: four composed schemas (core and Playlist Extension v0.2.0, whole-playlist and single-item) all referencing schema.json#/$defs/PlaylistItemExtension; fixtures under examples/ including rejected/ mutations.
Content Rating extension: consumer rules documented (filtering as consumer policy, unsigned projections, contentBlocked reserved, non-aware consumers accept and ignore).
Content Rating extension: audience suitability reserved for a separate future audience field; contentRating remains an exclusion label only.

Playlist extension: playlist_item_with_extension.json now enforces inlineManifest. The single-item composed schema hand-copied the per-item overlay and listed only note and displayAt, so a dynamicQuery item with a malformed inline Ref Manifest passed validation despite the §3.6 MUST; the whole-playlist path was unaffected.

Playlist extension: the per-item overlay is defined once as schema.json#/$defs/PlaylistItemExtension and referenced by both composed schemas, so the whole-playlist and single-item validation paths can no longer drift apart.
Playlist extension: §4.5.1 field list and Validation path prose corrected to name inlineManifest; extension version remains draft v0.2.0 and no schema $id changed.

Playlist extension: optional inlineManifest on each PlaylistItem — a complete Ref Manifest document inline, validated by the unmodified ref-manifest schema; ref overrides inlineManifest when both are present; inline bytes are covered by the DP-1 playlist signature so no refHash is required.
Playlist extension: validated via the extension fragment and composed playlist schema (allOf); canonical core playlist.json unchanged; status remains draft extension v0.2.0.
Playlist extension: bump to v0.2.0 (minor additive release).

Playlist extension: item-level displayAt (ISO 8601 subset; local datetime or RFC 3339 date-time; date-only not accepted) for time-based playback filtering; activates automatically when any item has displayAt (immediate apply on threshold; display locale for bare local).
Playlist extension: DisplayAt schema uses oneOf with mutually exclusive patterns (local datetime / date-time with bounded offset; portable without Format-Assertion).
Playlist extension: document timezone and DST gap/fold rules, playback eligibility and transition rules, Favorites strip guidance, and independence of displayAt from dynamicQuery item sourcing.
Playlist extension: add examples/daily-by-display-at.json Daily playlist example.
Registry: Playlist Extension version, resource URLs, description, and features list updated for displayAt scheduling (draft v0.2.0).
Channel extension: `publisher` is a valid `signatures[].role` value in schema.json; registry description and features updated.
Channel extension: documented player norm—verify at least one `feed` and one `publisher` signature before treating a channel as valid; rule remains prose-only (not enforced by JSON Schema).

Playlist extension: optional experimental Note object on playlist and on each PlaylistItem (text required up to 500 characters; duration optional, default 20 seconds when omitted) for intermission-style screens between works.
Playlist extension: Note is validated only via the extension fragment and composed playlist schema (allOf); canonical core playlist.json unchanged.
Registry: Playlist Extension description and features list updated to document Note; status remains draft extension v0.1.0.
Playlist extension: document composed full-playlist validator at playlist_with_extension.json (allOf bundled core-compatible playlist + extension fragment).
Playlist extension: add bundles/playlist-core-v1.1.0.json so validation allows an empty items array when dynamicQuery is present, without changing the canonical core playlist schema.
Playlist extension: registry resources include composedPlaylistSchema pointing at the composed schema URL for implementers and SDKs.
Initial registry release
Registered Channel Extension v1.0.0
Registered Playlist Extension v0.1.0
